players.product: antibody discovery and multispecific T-cell engager platform

quarterly_data.signal: ABCL635 Phase 2 clinical update deck (Exhibit 99.2, data cutoff 30JUL26) adds to the same-day top-line release: 92 patients enrolled versus N ~ 80 planned (N=46 per arm); a mean placebo-adjusted frequency difference of 2.6 already at week 1; mean severity at week 4 of 1.0 (mild) on ABCL635 versus 2.1 (moderate) on placebo; 87.0% of ABCL635 patients had a >50% reduction in frequency at week 4 (placebo 32.6%) and 60.9% a >90% reduction (placebo 8.7%); a significant sleep (PROMIS-SD-SF-8b) treatment difference of -5.5 at week 4; 84% of ABCL635 patients rated symptoms 'Much Better' or 'Moderately Better' versus 27% on placebo. Safety: no SAEs or severe (Grade 3+) AEs in the ABCL635 group versus 1 SAE and 2 severe AEs on placebo; headache 28.2% versus 13.0%; no evidence of gastrointestinal toxicity; one mild transaminase increase on ABCL635 that resolved in one week; no liver safety signal observed to date.
quarterly_data.figure: week-1 difference 2.6; >50% frequency responders 87.0% vs 32.6%; sleep difference -5.5; PGI-C 84% vs 27%; no SAEs on ABCL635

quarterly_data.signal: Deck market sizing and next steps: management estimates ~12M women in the US experience moderate-to-severe VMS, >6M of whom seek treatment, and a $6B+ total addressable market for non-hormonal treatments assuming only small-molecule net-price parity of ~$5K per patient per year; VMS due to cancer treatment with hormone deprivation (breast, prostate and ovarian cancer) is a further population. Next steps: additional data at major medical conferences later this year, completion of the 12-week follow-up to support optimal dose selection, and regulatory interactions to discuss late-stage development in VMS due to menopause and oncology treatments.
quarterly_data.figure: ~12M US women with moderate-to-severe VMS; >6M seek treatment; $6B+ TAM at ~$5K per patient per year
